title: Silvergate Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Silvergate Health onboarding to Redwood Inference. Reviewed high-level onboarding plan, security requirements (SSO, KMS, SOC2), networking (VPC peering/test env), and pilot success criteria. Agreed next steps: share security docs, provision test VPC credentials, schedule technical deep dive for infra team next week, and start a 2-week pilot with a dedicated test pool.
topics: Security: SSO/SAML, KMS, data residency, SOC 2
Deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated vs private
Pilot scope: models, latency/cost SLOs, traffic patterns
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, ISO) and onboarding guide - Samir - by 2027-07-19
Customer to provide test VPC peering info and IAM user for pilot - Priya - by 2027-07-21

transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-07-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Samir Patel, Dana Li, Carla Mendes (Redwood) / Maya Thompson, Jon Reyes, Priya Kapoor, Leo Grant (Silvergate)

Auto-summary (brief): kickoff; security + network checklist; pilot scope agreed; next steps assigned.

[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about an hour. I'm Samir, I'm the account lead, and with me is Dana our SE and Carla our CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya Thompson: Good thanks, Maya here. Excited to get this rolling.
[00:15] Jon Reyes: Hi all, Jon, CTO. We're mainly here to make sure the infra side checks out.
[00:20] Priya Kapoor: Priya, DevOps. I'll be handling VPC/peering and credentials.
[00:25] Dana Li: Great, quick agenda — intros, run through security/networking, pick pilot scope, and define success criteria and timeline.
[00:33] Samir Patel: Yep, that sounds right. Quick note: this is an onboarding kickoff, not a sales demo, so we'll focus on practical tasks.
[00:40] Leo Grant: One ask up front: we want to measure latencies at peak and avg, and cost per 1k tokens, roughly.
[00:48] Samir Patel: Absolutely. We'll include cost telemetry and token breakdowns in the console.

[01:05] Dana Li: On the deployment side, we typically recommend one of two paths for a pilot: hosted with isolated project and RBAC, or a small dedicated pool — more predictable latency. For Silvergate given compliance notes, I'd suggest dedicated test pool.
[01:25] Priya Kapoor: We prefer dedicated if it avoids sending PHI out. We have strict egress rules.
[01:32] Samir Patel: Understood. We can do Dedicated in a private VPC or Redwood Private for full on-prem — but Private is heavier. For initial pilot, Dedicated with VPC peering is common.
[01:50] Jon Reyes: What's the difference operationally? I heard 'Redwood Private' and 'Redwood Dedicated' — please clarify.
[01:58] Dana Li: Sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity managed by Redwood but isolated to your account, accessible via VPC peering. Private is an installation of our control plane in your environment or VPC, for air-gapped or stricter controls. Private requires longer lead time.

[02:25] Maya Thompson: Security items we care about: SSO/SAML, KMS for keys, audit logs, and SOC 2 report. Also data residency options.
[02:35] Samir Patel: We'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs in the security pack. We support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys. For SSO, we support SAML with IdP just fine — Carla will help with SSO setup steps.
[02:50] Carla Mendes: Quick note, we've seen some customers refer to SAML as "sample" in notes — sorry, transcription. We'll provide a step-by-step SSO checklist.

[03:10] Priya Kapoor: Network-wise, what do you need? CIDR ranges, ingress/egress rules, peering?
[03:18] Dana Li: Exactly — CIDR, peering contact, and a test IAM user or temporary creds for setup. We'll give you the minimal ports and egress rules. Also note we use heavy TLS so keep firewall rules open for our control plane IPs.

[03:45] Samir Patel: For pilot sizing, Dana — what do you recommend?
[03:48] Dana Li: For initial latency tests and a small production-feel workload, I recommend 2 x A10-style GPUs (or similar), single dedicated pool. We'll set autoscale thresholds low. We'll enable KV (kay vee) cache and prefix caching to reduce token cost. Also quantization profiles depending on the model — we'll propose.
[04:10] Maya Thompson: Good. For models, we'll test embeddings + 1 chat model for customer support responses; baseline target is p95 < 400ms generation for short prompts.
[04:22] Dana Li: Okay p95 400ms is reasonable for a small context and proper batching turned off for low latency. We'll document tradeoffs — latency vs cost.

[05:00] Jon Reyes: On the security front, what about logging and audit retention? We need event logs for 12 months.
[05:08] Samir Patel: We provide audit logs with configurable retention; extended retention is an add-on. We'll include retention options and costs in the pack.
[05:18] Maya Thompson: Great. Also data handling: can we restrict raw logs from leaving our VPC?
[05:24] Dana Li: For Dedicated you can route logs to your Kinesis/Splunk via secure forwarders; Private gives even more controls. We'll include the runbooks.

[06:00] Priya Kapoor: Any gotchas on VPC peering? IP ranges colliding etc?
[06:06] Dana Li: Yes avoid overlapping CIDRs. We'll provide a list of recommended CIDRs and the peering workflow. Also note if you have strict egress rules, the control plane will need limited outbound access — we'll list specific hostnames/IPs.

[07:10] Samir Patel: Let's talk schedule. Pilot start target: 2027-07-26 for two weeks. That gives us time to exchange creds and set up. Does that work?
[07:20] Priya Kapoor: Yes that works for our infra calendar.
[07:24] Maya Thompson: We'll lock a model set and provide baseline data by 07-20.

[08:00] Dana Li: During the pilot we'll run a set of bench scripts to capture token-level cost, latency distribution, and cold vs warm starts. We'll share a spreadsheet for benchmarks.
[08:12] Leo Grant: Please include cost per 1k tokens metric — that's critical for our finance team.
[08:18] Samir Patel: Yep we'll include that plus per-route breakdowns in the console.

[09:00] Jon Reyes: Compliance: are audit trails tamper-evident? We need proof for auditors.
[09:07] Carla Mendes: Audit logs are SHA-sum signed and we can provide signed exports per request; we'll add that to the docs.

[09:30] Maya Thompson: One more thing — model pinning and rollout. We want to pin a model version and roll forward incrementally.
[09:36] Dana Li: Redwood supports model version pinning and canary rollouts. We'll walk through the console flows in the next session.

[10:00] Priya Kapoor: Any network testing we should run on our side beforehand?
[10:05] Dana Li: A simple traceroute to our control plane hosts and verifying TLS handshakes is helpful. We'll provide exact hosts and IPs.

[11:00] Samir Patel: Okay to recap quick: Redwood sends security pack + onboarding doc by tomorrow; Silvergate provides VPC info and models to test by 07-21; Redwood SE will run infra deep dive next week and provision the dedicated pilot pool for 07-26 start. Action items noted in the chat.
[11:25] Maya Thompson: Sounds good. Any blockers we foresee?
[11:30] Priya Kapoor: Only IAM/peering scheduling on our side, might need a two-day window to coordinate network changes.
[11:36] Samir Patel: We can work around that. We'll provide rollback instructions for peering.

[12:00] Jon Reyes: One last question on backups — if we do persistence for cache or KV store, how do backups work?
[12:07] Dana Li: We keep ephemeral KV cache by default; if you want persistent state, we'll discuss options — usually through customer-managed storage with lifecycle policies. We'll include details in the pilot playbook.

[12:45] Carla Mendes: I'll send the calendar invites for the infra deep dive and the follow-up checkpoint mid-pilot.
[12:52] Leo Grant: Thanks all.

[13:00] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and next steps. End of call.

Notes: occasional transcription quirks observed (e.g., "kay vee" for KV, "sock two" for SOC 2) and some speaker overlap near the end. Refer to shared drive links: onboarding guide https://redwood.ai/onboarding-guide and security pack https://redwood.ai/security-pack.
